model: Insurer FCFE at cost of equity on core net income (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payment expense EUR 92m FY2025 (AR FY2025 line 14789) is already expensed inside core net income, which is the flow anchor; no further deduction (would double-count). 0.8% of core NI.
inputs.share_count_basis: 380,418,897 registered shares less 176,699 treasury = 380.24m outstanding at 31 Dec 2025 (AR FY2025 lines 14574, 14596). Less ~6.25m for the EUR 2.5bn 2026 buy-back (FY2025 capital return, announced in AR FY2025 line 8618) at an assumed ~EUR 400 average = 374.0m. That buy-back is funded from FY2025 earnings and is NOT in the projected flows, so the share reduction is counted once. Held flat thereafter because future buy-backs are inside the distribution stream (charging them in both the flow and the share count would double-count). Diluted adds only 0.09m (EPS note). NB: the Metrics.csv shares_outstanding of 389.1m for FY2025 is NI/EPS-derived and ~9m too high.
inputs.base_revenue_note: Not revenue. FY2025 shareholders' core net income = core EPS EUR 28.61 x 382.87m weighted basic shares = EUR 10,955m (AR FY2025 lines 7986, 14270; management states EUR 11.1bn before the undated-sub-bond coupon adjustment). Reported NI attributable EUR 10,603m.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Distributable FCFE proxy: FY2025 dividend EUR 17.10 x ~380m = EUR 6.5bn plus EUR 2.5bn buy-back = ~EUR 9.1bn (83% of core NI).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in EUR, not WACC: 10y Bund ~2.7% + beta ~1.0 x ERP 5.5-6.0% = ~8.5% base. Bull 7.75% (AA-rated, 218% Solvency II, lowest-volatility large-cap European insurer); bear 9.5% (adds nat-cat / capital-markets drawdown premium).
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable; lease cost (lease liabilities EUR 2.45bn) is inside core net income.
inputs.nci_treatment: Core net income is attributable to shareholders, i.e. already after NCI (EUR 655m FY2025); no further adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: insurer -> FCFE at cost of equity via the component engine with net debt held at zero, following the house precedent for insurers (PRU, MET, GL, IAG.AX, LGEN.L). The skill's routing table lists 'BVPS compounding x exit P/B' for insurers; that is used here as a cross-check rather than the primary because IFRS 17 (FY2023) broke the equity series (FY2020 EUR 80.8bn IFRS 4 vs FY2025 EUR 62.7bn) and equity excludes the EUR 55.9bn CSM, so book is not where the value sits. ENGINE MAPPING: base_revenue = shareholders' core net income; ebitda_margin_path = total payout ratio (dividend + buy-back as % of core NI); SBC, D&A, capex, cash tax, lease and working capital set to zero because core NI is already post-tax, post-interest and post-SBC. Flow = distributable FCFE; discounted at cost of equity; net_debt = 0 (financial debt is operating funding of an insurer and is already charged in core NI; subtracting it again would double-count). CROSS-CHECK: BVPS EUR 165 (62,722 / 380.2), core RoE 18.1% -> justified P/B (RoE - g)/(CoE - g) = (18 - 3.5)/(8.5 - 3.5) = 2.9x -> ~EUR 480, vs market P/B 2.6x. Analysis JSON was not yet available at build time (concurrent agent); qualitative inputs taken from the FY2025 annual report outlook and the Q3-2025 presentation. No H1-2026 interim is extracted, so FY2026 is judged from guidance only.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: operating_profit_3yr_cagr (Allianz's headline metric, continuous across the IFRS 17 break)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR (-4.9%) diverges >30% from EPS 5y CAGR (11.1%): the IFRS 4 -> IFRS 17 transition in FY2023 moved CSM out of equity and the 2022 rate shock cut OCI. Revenue 3y/5y CAGRs are also break-distorted (FY2022 122.7bn IFRS 4 gross premiums vs FY2023 104.9bn insurance revenue + fees); the post-IFRS 17 2y revenue CAGR is 6.0%.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null by design: operating cash flow is dominated by policyholder and investment flows (FY2022 OCF 2.0bn vs FY2021 25.1bn) and no FCF is extracted. SBC is <1% of core NI and not a growth driver. DPS grew ~8%/yr 2015-2024 per AR FY2025.

base.growth_rates_rationale: Aggregate core NI growth (not EPS; buy-back accretion is in the distribution stream). FY2026: OP guided EUR 17.4bn +/-1bn (flat midpoint, Allianz habitually guides low and beat 2025 guidance) plus a higher L/H CSM release and lower share count -> +4% aggregate. 2027 at the low end of the 7-9% core EPS CAGR 2025-27 target less ~2.5% buy-back accretion. Fades to 3% as retention x RoE implies: 20% retention x 16-18% RoE = 3.2-3.6%.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: Total payout ratio of core NI. Capital Management Policy: 60% regular dividend + minimum 15% via buy-backs = 75% floor; actual FY2025 ~83% (EUR 6.5bn dividend + EUR 2.5bn buy-back). Base 80%, consistent with ~3.5% growth at 18% RoE.

scenario_narratives.base: Allianz delivers roughly its own plan: operating profit at the guided ~EUR 17.4bn in 2026 then mid-single-digit growth, P&C combined ratio held at 92-93%, L/H CSM release 8-9%, PIMCO/AllianzGI margins under passive pressure but flows positive. Core NI compounds ~4% in aggregate (7-8% per share with buy-backs) fading to 3%, with ~80% paid out. Cost of equity 8.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Pricing and productivity (AI, Allianz Direct, claims automation) push P&C combined ratio toward 91%, higher-for-longer rates lift the operating investment result and L/H new business (VNB EUR 4.8bn), and asset management returns to inflows. Core NI grows 7% near term (upper half of the 7-9% EPS target before buy-back accretion), payout 82%, and the market re-rates a 218%-solvency AA franchise toward a 7.75% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: A heavy nat-cat year (guidance assumes ~3% of NEP vs 1.4% in 2025) plus an equity/credit drawdown and a USD weakening (10% USD move is disclosed as material) cut 2026 core NI 3%; the Solvency II ratio falls toward the high-100s and buy-backs are trimmed to the 15% floor (payout 75%). PIMCO fee compression continues. Recovery to 2-3% growth; cost of equity 9.5%, terminal growth 2%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25. The balance sheet carries no solvency tail (218% SII vs 150% policy floor), which argues against a heavy bear weight, but an insurer's earnings carry fat-tailed nat-cat and capital-market risk that argues against tilting toward bull either; the stock is near the top of its 52-week range after a strong 2025.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Allianz is valued on what it can distribute to shareholders: core net income times a payout ratio set by its Capital Management Policy (60% dividend + >=15% buy-backs), discounted at a EUR cost of equity with no net-debt deduction. Owner FCF, EBITDA and net debt have no meaning for an insurer. Justified P/B on core RoE is the cross-check.
key_risks_to_valuation: Nat-cat severity above the ~3% of NEP budget (climate-driven frequency, U.S. and European convective storms).
Capital-market drawdown: equity/credit/spread shocks hit the Solvency II ratio and could pause buy-backs; distributions are discretionary.
Asset management fee compression at PIMCO and AllianzGI from passive products; outflows in a bond bear market.
USD/EUR translation: guidance assumes 1.17; a 10% USD move is disclosed as material to operating profit.
Cost-of-equity sensitivity: each 50bp on CoE moves the base value ~10%.
Litigation tail (Structured Alpha precedent) and regulatory interference (German/EU tax, Solvency II review).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 338.8-454.6
data_sources.financials: Allianz Annual Report FY2025 (core EPS, EPS note, share capital, capital management policy, outlook 2026), Q3-2025 presentation (2025-27 targets), ALV.DE_Metrics.csv kpis (OperatingProfit, SolvencyRatio, DividendsPaid, ShareRepurchases)
